posts.title: Manuel was annoyed
posts.description: The reason I dug into the translation settings in the first place was this popup – it keeps coming up after dismissing it. Not every time, but frequently enough to be really annoying. There appears to be no way to disable it.

posts.title: Manuel was annoyed
posts.description: Your browser does not support the video tag. I never again want to hear a single word about the Windows settings mixing different generations’ UI styles. (This is in the as-of-writing latest macOS version 27.0.1, which is still an inexcusable crime against taste. [The weird artifacts in the video are courtesy of macOS’ screen recording functionality – it’s not in the actual UI.])

posts.title: Manuel was annoyed
posts.description: A story in three screenshots: What a weird requirement. Of course the two “different” languages were “English (US)” and “English (UK)”, despite me never having explicitly configured the latter – I assume that Apple just presumes this based on geo-location when you set Siri to English while in Europe? Five minutes later, first hurdle overcome: how big is this download? How long will it take? How fast is it downloading? Five and a half hours later, absolutely zero indication if anything is actually happening or not. The download had finished the next morning. I don’t even have interest in ever using this app, I just can’t help myself from following through with crap like this when I encounter it.
